title: Low-Latency Cipher with Efficient Threshold Masking
summary: Proper threshold masking is incompatible with fully unrolled architectures; it remains open to design a strong cipher that is low-latency unrolled and efficiently masked when round-based.

formal_statement.body: A cipher-design gap remains: construct a cryptographically strong cipher that has low latency in both fully unrolled and round-based implementations, while also admitting a threshold-implementation-masked round-based implementation that is efficient in both area and latency for applications requiring provably secure side-channel-analysis protection.

scope.domain: Block-cipher design for low-latency hardware and threshold-implementation side-channel protection.
parameters: Implementation architecture: fully unrolled and round-based forms are both subject to latency requirements
Area and latency: efficiency measures for the threshold-masked round-based implementation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a cryptographically strong cipher meeting both latency goals and providing an area- and latency-efficient threshold-masked round-based implementation for provably secure side-channel protection.

citations.label: Side-Channel Analysis Protection and Low-Latency in Action - - Case Study of PRINCE and Midori -

progress.summary: After analyzing PRINCE and Midori, the paper explicitly presents a “gap to fill” and does not claim a construction meeting the complete target.
